sections.title: Automatic build and publish
sections.what: On pushes to main or dev and pull requests to main, builds the backend image. Publishes the image as latest on Docker Hub only for pushes, not pull requests.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the build checked and a published copy available. The build cache likely speeds up later builds.
sections.watch_out: A dev push overwrites latest, and the shared deploy group can cancel a running main build.

summary: An automated workflow that builds the backend container image on pushes and pull requests, and publishes it to Docker Hub on pushes.
purpose: Checks that the backend still builds and keeps a published copy of the latest image.
why: Likely reason: automating the build catches breakage early. The build cache likely speeds up repeat builds.
how: Runs on each push to main or dev and each pull request to main. Checks out the code, sets up the builder, logs in to Docker Hub for non-pull-request events, then builds the backend image and pushes it with the latest tag when not a pull request.
inputs: Code from the repository and the Docker Hub username and password secrets.
outputs: A built image, and on pushes a published image tagged latest on Docker Hub.
risks: Pushes to dev also overwrite the latest tag. The shared deploy group cancels a running build when a new one starts, so a dev push can cancel a main build.
debug: If the build fails, read the build step log. If login fails, check the secrets. If latest is wrong, check which branch last pushed.
